name: Venus Pipes & Tubes Ltd
tagline: Well-run, backward-integrated stainless-steel pipe maker taking organised-sector share with ~21% ROCE and a record Q1 FY27 - but management itself guides only ~20% revenue CAGR, so the upside slope is a compounder's, not a 10x/2-3yr
business_overview: Venus Pipes & Tubes (incorporated 2015) manufactures seamless and welded stainless-steel pipes and tubes from a single integrated facility in Bhavnagar, Gujarat, selling into oil & gas, power, petrochemicals, pharma, food & beverage, chemicals and engineering, and exporting to 30+ countries (Europe and the US the largest). The model is backward integration - buying stainless round bars and piercing them into hollows - to capture higher EBITDA/kg. It is expanding into pipe fittings, stainless-titanium welded tubes, and additional seamless capacity (Phase 1 fittings in H1 FY26, Phase 2 seamless by Dec 2025), and has an LOI-stage optionality in data-centre piping / spooling.
fundamentals_table: FY26 ~+22% to ~Rs 1,167 Cr; ~40% revenue CAGR (multi-year); Q1 FY27 record ~Rs 320 Cr (+16% YoY)
~20% revenue/EBITDA CAGR to FY27; EBITDA margin target 18%+ by FY27 (currently ~16%)
Credit rating upgraded to IVR A/Stable; heavy capex phase; elongated operating cycle / high receivables
fundamentals_narrative: A quality small-cap: ~21% ROCE, ~17% ROE, consistent ~20%+ volume growth, backward integration lifting EBITDA/kg, exports up to ~one-third of revenue at higher margins, and a rating upgrade. Q1 FY27 was a record top line (~Rs 320 Cr, +16% YoY) led by a ~31% jump in domestic sales (power, chemicals, engineering, oil & gas), though exports contracted that quarter. The consistent knock is weak operating cash conversion versus reported profit during the capex/inventory build, and margins that sit at ~16% versus a stated 18%+ target.
technical_read: Not independently pulled. Thread history shows a repeating ~25% correction-then-recovery pattern (Rs 1,600 high -> Rs 1,200 in 2023; Rs 2,450 -> ~Rs 1,821 in late 2024), currently ~Rs 1,658 within a Rs 888-1,875 band. One member's rule-of-thumb: it has historically doubled within a year off each ~25% drawdown.
sentiment_summary: Read the most recent 50 of 68 posts, May 2023 to Aug 2026. Long-running, high-quality thread. The consistent bull case: multiple simultaneous levers - 30%+ volume growth, 300 bps margin expansion from backward integration, anti-dumping/anti-subsidy duties on Chinese/Vietnamese SS pipe, a structural unorganised->organised shift (only ~3 major organised players holding ~30% share), promoter warrant subscription at Rs 1,700, and product-mix shift toward higher-margin seamless. Recurring bear/caution points: valuation never cheap (PE ~35x on forward earnings at various points), receivables more than doubling FY23->FY24, weak cash from operations vs operating profit, and margins drifting to ~16-18% from a ~20% peak. Recent posts (Jun-Aug 2026): abhay.jain and kdjolly posted detailed notes; the Q1 FY27 concall summary highlights record revenue, domestic dominance (71% of revenue), debt reduction and interest-cost reduction as the near-term focus, with revenue growth of at least 20% and margin expansion to ~18% cited as the share-price trigger, plus a fast-tracked data-centre piping opportunity as a possible new driver. karanshah137 (elevated-tier) flagged the data-centre LOI in May 2026 as interesting optionality (explicitly 'LOI not a firm order').
community_signal: No core-tier roster user. Elevated-tier karanshah137 posted informational optionality context (data-centre LOI), not a conviction call. The most-loved posts (Shikhar 9, Vinay_Garg 10, Chirayu_Shah 9 concall notes, cdas3317 9 tracking template, sumitjain0014 9) are analytical and constructively positive but none is a fresh high-conviction buy call at the current price.

Credit rating upgraded (Infomerics) to IVR A/Stable long-term, IVR A1 short-term (Oct 2024). bull_case: ~21% ROCE / ~17% ROE with ~20%+ consistent volume growth and a multi-year ~40% revenue CAGR
Backward integration and product-mix shift to seamless lift EBITDA/kg; exports at ~one-third of revenue carry a 2-4% margin premium
Structural unorganised-to-organised share shift in SS pipe, aided by anti-dumping/anti-subsidy duties on Chinese/Vietnamese imports; only ~3 organised players
Capacity roughly doubling via Phase 1/2 (fittings, SS-titanium, seamless); new data-centre piping / spooling optionality; debt and interest cost falling
Consistent, credible management execution and a credit-rating upgrade
bear_case: Management guides only ~20% revenue/EBITDA CAGR - a compounder's slope, not a 10x-in-2-3-years slope
Valuation has never been cheap (PE ~35x forward at various points); much of the growth is habitually priced in
Weak operating cash conversion versus reported profit; receivables more than doubled FY23->FY24; elongated operating cycle during the capex phase
Margins at ~16% versus the stated 18%+ FY27 target; steel-realisation and raw-material swings drive quarterly volatility (Q1 FY27 exports contracted)
Cyclical end-markets; a bigger competitor (Ratnamani) and a converging one (Dee Development) in the same space
verdict_headline: A genuinely good, well-run compounder - filtered out only because ~20% guided growth does not reach the 10x-in-2-3-years or 100x-in-10-years bar, not for any quality weakness
verdict_reasoning: Quality gate is clearly met (~21% ROCE, real ~20%+ volume growth, backward integration, rating upgrade) - this is not a weak-fundamentals rejection

It is an upside-slope rejection: management's own ~20% revenue CAGR guidance, a habitually full valuation, and only ~16% margins mean the realistic outcome is steady compounding, not a 10x in 2-3 years; the data-centre piping LOI is optionality, not yet a thesis-changer

Not in the old 108-stock project. Conviction MEDIUM as a quality name; thesis-fit 'neither'. Re-check if the data-centre opportunity converts to firm orders large enough to re-slope growth well above 20%

four_box.note: Unorganised-to-organised SS-pipe share shift + anti-dumping duties (only ~3 organised players) is a real structural tailwind; management's own ~20% revenue/EBITDA CAGR guidance is explicitly 'a compounder's slope, not a 10x-in-2-3-years slope' — tam no; backward integration + seamless mix-shift lifting EBITDA/kg is a genuine moat; ~35x forward P/E 'never cheap... much of the growth is habitually priced in' — valuation no.

market_expectation.implied_growth_cagr: ~35x forward P/E on ~20% management-guided revenue CAGR is materially full for a small-cap compounder; implies either faster growth (data-centre opportunity) or margin expansion (to 18%+) is required to justify the valuation

market_expectation.our_fy28_estimate: Revenue +18-22% (Rs 1,650-1,800 Cr growth moderating), EBITDA margin reaches 18%+ target, PAT +15-20%; data-centre opportunity (if firm orders materialize) could add 5-10% upside to growth
market_expectation.gap_basis: The consistent ~35x forward P/E valuation across multiple points in the thread history (never cheap) means much of the ~20% guided growth is already baked in; valuation upside requires either the data-centre LOI converting to large firm orders or EBITDA margins compressing expectations further
